schema: houseCARL skill evals, 2026-09 convention (rewrite ruling 3): one file, evals.json; every trigger eval carries a without-skill arm; every run executes from the packaged tree.
never_run_from: .claude/skills/ (the source tree ships a different set of files: evals/ and dev-side ledgers are pruned at package time, so a source-tree run does not measure what a user loads)
rerun_rule: Run the full suite (both arms of both sets) before promoting a version or building a release package. Not 'only if the description text changes' — that narrow rule let nine unresolvable reference paths ship through every release since the last description change.
capability_statement_anonymized: A specialized capability for authoring, building, and auditing NATIVE SKSE PLUGIN DLLs for Skyrim — C++ code compiled against the CommonLibSSE(-NG) library into a .dll that loads under SKSE. In scope: writing a new SKSE plugin from scratch (plugin lifecycle, event sinks that react to game events, code hooks/trampolines that patch the running game), inventing a brand-new native Papyrus function — BOTH its C++ registration and its .psc declaration, setting up the C++ build toolchain (MSVC/CMake/vcpkg) for such a project, making one DLL run across Skyrim SE/AE/VR (Address Library, multi-runtime discipline), and reading someone else's open-source SKSE plugin source to explain what its compiled DLL does. OUT OF SCOPE: editing record data in .esp/.esm files (armor/weapon/NPC/dialogue records), merging or ESL-flagging .esp plugins, writing ordinary .psc Papyrus scripts against functions that already exist, authoring distributor config files (SPID/KID/SkyPatcher .ini), diagnosing a user's game crash from a crash log, and end-user SKSE installation.

trigger_set.purpose: Does the description route the right requests here and keep the wrong ones out?

method.shape: Anonymized fresh-agent relevance fan-out: one fresh-context agent per query per run, each shown the lettered menu of all shipped skill descriptions (this skill unflagged) plus NONE, asked which ONE to load. Adjudicated on the agent's reasoning, not on the verdict token.
method.without_skill_arm: The same query, the same menu with this skill's entry removed, in a fresh context. A positive row that is answered correctly without the skill is evidence the skill is not earning that row; a negative row that goes wrong only in the with-skill arm is a false-trigger cost.
method.held_out_ids_note: The only record of the split — 8 of 20, matching split.held_out, 3 positives and 5 negatives. Rows carry no held_out flag of their own; a second copy is the one that drifts. Row 6 is deliberately not here: the description was fitted to it (see its note), so held-out membership would count a trained row toward the generalization score. Row 8 takes the slot — a positive this rewrite aimed no edit at. REWRITE.md:483-486 held row 6 out on the ground that it was 'not used to tune the text'; that ground did not survive, so the row moves rather than the claim.
method.deployment_envelope: If a model is skipped, the record states which models the result holds for rather than generalizing.
method.coexistence_note: The coexistence set must include a query that exercises what used to be the papyrus-reference handoff — a new native's .psc declaration — because that is this skill's real coexistence risk now that it owns both halves. It is the row below rather than a 21st entry in evals, which stays at 10 positives and 10 negatives.

coexistence_set.query: i'm adding a native to my SKSE dll — what does the .psc declaration for it look like on the script side?
coexistence_set.why: The half this skill newly owns. papyrus-reference is a lookup corpus for functions that exist, so it can only warn; a pick of it is the pre-rewrite failure reproducing.

method.row_record: Every row records passed (bool) and evidence (a quoted phrase from the agent's reasoning), never a bare label.

Scoring it against a fresh control would measure the old skill while claiming to measure the new one. Both arms are re-run together, from the packaged tree, at the rewrite commit.

without_skill.status: missing — this is the control the 2026-09 eval graded as absent, and running it is what turns the skill's value from self-report into a measurement

predictions.expectation: The control pins the frozen CharmedBaryon fork — a commonlibsse-ng vcpkg dependency plus a registry entry — rather than the alandtse ng git submodule.
The control omits /Zc:preprocessor, or the force-included PCH carrying the game headers, and debugs the resulting error backwards.
The control assumes a dual SE+AE build defines EXCLUSIVE_SKYRIM_SE and EXCLUSIVE_SKYRIM_AE rather than EXCLUSIVE_SKYRIM_FLAT alone.
The control writes SKSE::Init(a_skse) after setting up logging and loses every pre-Init log line.
The control emits both a hand-written SKSEPluginInfo block and add_commonlibsse_plugin, giving duplicate exports.
The control returns size_t, int64 or double from the native and takes the silent truncation.

output_quality_set.pass_condition: At least one expectation passes with the skill and fails without it. The skill loses any prediction the control gets right unaided.

cost.why: Cost is part of the verdict on a skill carrying 266 KB of references — the with-skill audit spent about half its reading volume on material the job did not touch.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.method: Revalidation for issue #294 (all 13 descriptions compressed to the amended 200-400 char target): fan-out with one fresh-context sonnet agent per query, each shown the full lettered menu of the 13 new descriptions plus NONE; one opus adjudicator per skill scored from reasoning.

misses.query: here's the github for an open-source combat overhaul's SKSE dll. can you read the source and tell me what it actually patches in the engine
misses.diagnosis: The description's verbs read as first-party production work — "Author, build, or audit ... Use for writing or building an SKSE plugin" — so the agent scoped "audit" to auditing one's own plugin and concluded reading a third party's DLL source was uncovered; the body's "or read one" never reaches the trigger surface.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.adjudicator_notes: Recall 9/10 (0.90 >= 0.80), specificity 10/10 (1.00 >= 0.50) — PASS. No reasoning-vs-token overrides needed: every pick token matched its stated reasoning, including row 6, where the agent explicitly reasoned this skill out of scope rather than mis-typing. Specificity was clean with no near-misses, and the .esp/.psc disambiguation clause appears to be doing that work (rows 12, 14, 17, 20 all routed to data-layer or Papyrus entries without SKSE confusion). Only actionable fix: surface read/reverse-engineer coverage in the trigger sentence (e.g. "reading or auditing someone else's SKSE DLL source"), since the body claims it and the description did not. That fix is applied in the 2026-09 rewrite.
revalidation_2026-07-28_294.contamination_audit_2026-07-28: PR #295 review follow-up: the independent review found adjudicator notes quoting text that exists only in the pre-compression descriptions. Forensics on the run journal established: (a) judges were shown the new menu; (b) 11 of 281 judge rows leaked old description text from the agents' own environment skill listing into their reasoning; (c) some adjudicator notes confabulated 'verbatim quotes' from that same stale environment. All contaminated rows were re-judged with a hardened prompt: 15/15 confirmed their original verdicts, except dialogue-authoring q19, whose recorded miss was itself a contamination artifact and is overturned. Treat quoted description text in the run-1 notes as unreliable where it does not appear in the shipped description; scores are pick-derived and were confirmed by the hardened re-run.
